When `POST /articles` is called, the `create_new_article` function in `app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py` is executed [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:53].

This function performs the following steps:
1.  It takes an `article_create` body (which must contain an `article` field) and the currently authenticated `user` [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:60, E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:61].
2.  It depends on an `ArticlesRepository` instance, which is obtained via `get_repository(ArticlesRepository)` [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:62].
3.  It calculates the `slug` for the article using `get_slug_for_article(article_create.title)` [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:64].
4.  It checks if an article with that `slug` already exists by calling `check_article_exists(articles_repo, slug)` [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65]. If it exists, it raises an `HTTPException` with status code 400 [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:66].
5.  If the article does not exist, it calls `articles_repo.create_article(...)` to create the article, passing the calculated `slug`, `title`, `description`, `body`, the `user` as the author, and the `tags` [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:71-78].
6.  Finally, it returns an `ArticleInResponse` object, constructed from the newly created `article` using `ArticleForResponse.from_orm(article)` [E2, app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:79].
